title: High Order Roe-WENO Schemes Based on Higher-Order Central Differencing and Reconstruction
text:
Overview
This thesis investigates two approaches to developing higher-order shock-capturing schemes based on Roe’s approximate Riemann solver.
The first approach increases the order of the left and right state reconstruction using weighted essentially non-oscillatory (WENO) methods. These reconstructed states are used in both the average and diffusive contributions to the numerical flux.
The second approach applies higher-order central differencing to the average-flux contribution while retaining higher-order reconstruction for the diffusive contribution.
Both approaches are evaluated by solving the unsteady, one-dimensional compressible Euler equations for four Riemann-problem configurations.

title: High Order Roe-WENO Schemes Based on Higher-Order Central Differencing and Reconstruction
text:
Research Background
This work was completed in 2021 for the Master of Science in Engineering program in Mechanical Engineering at the University of Alabama in Huntsville.
Author: Joshua A. Fowler
Department: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
The numerical solver was developed from scratch to investigate how reconstruction and flux formulation affect solution accuracy, numerical diffusion, and stability.

title: High Order Roe-WENO Schemes Based on Higher-Order Central Differencing and Reconstruction
text:
Methods Investigated
The thesis develops and examines:

Finite-volume discretization of the compressible Euler equations.
Roe’s approximate Riemann solver.
The Harten–Hyman entropy fix.
MUSCL reconstruction.
Third-order and fifth-order WENO reconstruction.
Higher-order central-differencing modifications.
Explicit temporal discretization, including an SSP Runge–Kutta method.

title: High Order Roe-WENO Schemes Based on Higher-Order Central Differencing and Reconstruction
text:
Benchmark Problems
The methods are evaluated using four configurations:

Modified Sod shock tube.
Blast wave.
Shock collision.
Stationary contact wave.

The comparisons examine how the schemes resolve shocks, contact discontinuities, and other high-gradient features.

title: High Order Roe-WENO Schemes Based on Higher-Order Central Differencing and Reconstruction
text:
Main Findings
For the configurations examined, increasing the order of reconstruction reduced numerical diffusion and improved the resolution of high-gradient regions.
The alternative approach using higher-order central differencing in the average-flux contribution produced unstable behavior and large oscillations in high-gradient regions for most test cases.
The thesis discusses these results in the context of the interaction between reconstruction, numerical dissipation, and flux formulation.

Related Software
The Euler solver has been implemented independently in several scientific computing languages:

MATLAB — HighOrderEuler-MATLAB
C++ — HighOrderEuler-Cpp
Python — PyHighOrderEuler
Julia — HighOrderEuler.jl

These repositories provide related implementations. Their current contents may differ from the software version used for the original thesis.
